comment: Not accessible. Takes off points for basically anything. I ended with an A because at the very end he made it easy, but the class was challenging up until that point. Homework was pretty irrelevant and his lectures made no sense. Sit in the front to hear him.
Didn't learn any math, an easy class to get a good grade in but if you want to go into calc2 you won't have any background if you take this professor. The final exam was a group presentation.

If you want to deal with inaccessible office hours, and unclear grading then this is the class for you.The professors voice is so monotone that it will put you to sleep. It is also very quiet. You need to sit at the front to hear him. I asked for office hours multiple times throughout the semester and it was very difficult to schedule it with him.

Took Calc in HS - not doing well in class. I've already written a review, and I feel compelled to send another warning. If you care about your well-being, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.
Learning targets are comically difficult to meet. You have to explain (physically write) how you know what you are doing - forget a key word, whole section is wrong.

Very nice guy, ALWAYS willing to meet outside of class, but I'd never take his class again. Tests are 99% of the grade and unlike anything I've taken before, conceptual, not math-heavy, but extremely difficult. You must write exactly what he wants to get credit. You will retake previous exams on the next exam for missed credit, but still hard to do

Do not take this teacher. He met with me once and it was because I triple emailed and asked him to make time after class. Otherwise very unresponsive. Content is made up. None of the helpers in the math help center knew what he was talking about.

He's a nice guy, but I learn more from the person who sits next to me. Tests are not too hard, but they're graded pass fail, so if you miss one little thing, you have to retake whole parts of the test.

Even in the front row, he is almost impossible to pay attention to, his pacing during lectures is cartoonishly slow, and much of the content is simply made up. He grades tests by sections consisting of multiple problems, and if you get one of these problems wrong, he gives you an N on the entire section. Won't wish him on anyone but my worst enemy.
DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR PLEASE SAVE YOURSELF

He is extremely unresponsive to emails; I constantly have to triple email him to ask for office hours (he usually doesn't respond or say yes). He is a harsh grader and has a weird grading policy. Many students in class have failed his tests, and struggle to hit all of his "learning targets." His classes are also slow and make absolutely 0 sense.

Dr. Caudill is a slow lecturer, but he walks through examples and covers what will be on the tests. If you put any amount of effort, you'll be fine. There are 3 group mini-projects and a final 20-minute group presentation. If you miss a question on one of the tests, just meet with him and he'll tell you exactly how to get it right next time.

Dr. Cuadill's intention to reduce the stress by implementing a categorical grading system is thoughtful but it is also challenging for students. Overall, I loved Dr. C and he was a great lecturer that always sprinkled comedy into class. His projects were extremely organized and interesting. I would take him again, despite some grading frustration.

I initially thought his grading system was designed to help student's grades but it was the complete opposite. The lectures were very average. The mini-projects are interesting and his instructions for assignments are very organized; he is also a nice guy. One more thing, he has a horrible handwriting so lecture notes are unreadable.
Not worth the hours I spent trying to make sure my assignments met his ridiculous grading scale. He doesn't emulate the kind of responses he requires, so you just have to be excessively thorough.

Don't take him unless it's a major requirement. Generally, he's nice and a fine lecturer but does not demonstrate the same level of thoroughness in answers that he seems to require for full points. More interested giving you the least amount of credit on your answers possible than actually making sure you understand the process.

If you can avoid him, do it. He gives homework pretty frequently however infrequently returns them graded. I never received several assignments and had no idea what grade I was going to get until the final grades were released. Do not recommend.

Good luck. Maybe if you laugh at his jokes, he'll grade you less harshly. You won't have any idea of what your grade is going into the final project. His inability to grade in a timely manner is almost comical.

If you'd like to see a terrible implementation of a mastery based grading scale, please go ahead and take this course. Six criteria to "master" with little practical feedback and lectures not focused on application, but rather tangents and long-winded perspectives of the material will make one regret taking this class.

I do not understand how a 300 level course has such as intensely atrocious grading scale. Do not expect timely feedback, if any feedback at all. Expect all grading to be interested in taking off the maximum number of points possible. Do not expect you learning the material to be a priority. Expect to feel regret over this course.

If you want to receive feedback on graded work in a reasonable time frame or have a lecture that moves faster than a glacial pace while actually teaching you the material, I do not recommend Dr. Caudill. His grading scale is needlessly convoluted, amplified by his inability to grade in a timely manner and his ruthlessness in taking off points.

By far the most confusing and worst grading scale I have ever encountered. 3rd to last week of semester and still haven't received assignments back from 2nd week into classes which leads to many repeat errors since you never get feedback on work in time - rare feedback is also very convoluted and is always looking for excuses to take points off.

Dr. Caudill is very intelligent but not the best when it comes to teaching.  What could be an extremely basic problem or equation becomes a two-lecture long tangent. I ended up having to teach myself a lot of the work. I would not suggest him although he is a great guy.

Caudill can be funny sometimes, but he's a pretty standard lecturer. Nothing special, and the homework is manageable but sometimes he throws in a super hard question and doesn't really ever explain how to do it (before or after). Calc2 is a hard subject, and he tries his best to explain everything. He isn't great at responding to emails.

I don’t know why, but I can’t really focus when he is lecturing. Grading is great, but I was worried for participation for a little bit. Definitely learned a lot from the group projects, and most importantly, I still know enough vocab out of the class to figure out how to teach myself again.

Dr. Caudill is a pretty decent lecturer, and he does seem to take student input into account for things like due dates. My only complaint is the grading system. I made an M (meets expectations) on a quiz and had no idea what grade I would have in the class since many of the other assignments were graded late. He doesn't deserve less than a 3.

Not sure, but I think I got a B in his class. Really nice guy, but not a good teacher. Grades homework assignments for accuracy rather than completion and I often had to go to one of the other professors in the department for help because he would not help me. Final exam contained material that was not covered in class or on previous tests.

He is a very caring and sweet prof, but the way he teaches isn't ideal. He tends to overcomplicate simple concepts, and I felt like we were behind all semester. I would not recommend taking his class if you want to take any higher-level math after it.

Not the most interesting professor I have had, but he is one of the nicest guys. Calculus was probably the most high school-esque class here that I have taken so far, it's not bad if you've taken it in high school as it is pretty much review. Coursework isn't unbearable.

A lot of these reviews are negative towards him and say that he doesn't teach well, but honestly if you pay attention in class and ask any questions you have after class then you will do fine. He is one of the nicest teachers I've ever had and he really cares about his students.

If you did not take Calc in high school DO NOT take this class. Homework assignments are unnecessarily long and do not relate to class. I struggled on every homework assignment, each taking hours to complete. He's a really nice guy and tries to be interesting and is a pretty generous grader.

If you took calculus in high school, you can maybe get an A or B+ if the material comes back to you. If you didn't take calc in high school, this class will be awful. He spends half of the class going over science problems that interest him and rarely explains or practices the material that's on the long hw assignments. Really caring guy, though.

Dr. Caudill mainly teaches high level calc, and he is just too smart to teach lower levels. A lot of real world application to his class! He is a great guy, very caring and forgiving, but be prepared to work. HW about 75% of the time, and tests that aren't too difficult if you put in the effort. Most forgiving grader I've had for a math class!!!

Possibly the worst teacher I've ever had. He doesn't teach during class and assigns homework that you have no idea how to do. Would not take another class of his in a million years. Couldn't rate him a 0, Nice guy though.

Dr Caudill breaks down the class material in a good way which helps me understand the material better. His exams are not easy but fair. Everything will be what he talked about in class. There is a lot of homework. Group projects are somewhat fun, but he's requirement is kinda vague. He is definitely a tough grader, but it's still possible to get A

Dr. Caudill's teaching is average. He uses a program called DyKnow, a shared whiteboard, and so you don't need to take any notes, but that was actually not beneficial after all. There is also lots of HW, but he doesn't provide the necessary methodology to solve it during lectures, so you're gonna have to teach yourself through the textbook.

Dr. Caudill is very nice in person, helpful and very dedicated to students. His lectures are clear with good speed. Homework are close to exams, so you will not need to study extra materials besides understanding all homework problems. Also mathematica is a very very useful tool, definitely worth learning it!

I enjoy Dr. Caudill as a person, but LA with him is pretty weird. You mostly have to teach yourself from the book, and lengthy homework is assigned after every class. When he does teach (usually the concepts you did in HW), his explanations can be unintuitive and needlessly abstracted. Really nice guy though, and I would be ok taking him again.

Lots of homework; each assignment will take a couple hours on average. He assigns homework after every class, which equates to a lot of hours spent on homeworks. Not my preference, but some people may learn better this way, idk. I definitely learned a lot from the class, but some concepts are still blurry for me. Tests are straightforward.

Dr. Caudill is a dedicated, thoughtful teacher. If you struggle with anything, he is very welcoming and will help answer any questions you have. If you don't pay attention in class, don't take notes, don't turn in assignments or aren't responsive in class, you'll have a hard time earning a good grade. Otherwise, you'll have a fantastic time!

I don't understand all of these shades thrown at Dr. C. He is kind, caring, funny and very receptive to questions. I love his class and would love to take him again. Plus honestly if you whine because of too much work, you prolly are not hard working enough and don't have good work ethic. Don't expect any college class to be easy and work hard!

Doesn't explain the material logic, doesn't even cover the material or examples properly. Horrible at teaching, he uses computers to explain math which is very ineffective and his tests are unreasonably hard since you have to learn everything by your own.

Probably the most useless Professor I've had. The frustration with this class did not come from his ability to teach the material; it came from him just not teaching it. The notes he provides in class are not sufficient to do the homework; you have to learn concepts by reading a textbook. This class wasted so much of my time.
Dumps assignments on you every class, isn't very clear, and not very helpful.

Comes off as a very friendly guy, but his class will ruin your life.  Attendance isn't mandatory...but homework that he claims is "graded periodically" is really due and graded every single class.  And by no means is the homework easy/quick to accomplish.  I would advise anyone to drop this class or switch professors.

Do not let the positive comments lead you to believe that Caudill is funny or charming in the way that some other dorky, math-loving teachers can be. His humor is lame. His class is boring. Even though he often speaks at a mind-numbingly slow pace, he still manages to make the material seem more confusing than it is.
Caudil sometimes comes off as cold, but he's actually pretty friendly during class. He does a good job connecting the material to real world examples, and overall I'd take his class over many others.

I was surprised he got so many negative comments, but i can see where they were coming from. granted, he's not the most fun and affable teacher ever, but if you ask him the right questions he can answer your question. however he's only warm towards math experts so he may seem cold and incomprehensible to normal people. tests are easy though.

single-handedly destroyed my GPA. if you like math and you're decent at it, take him, you'll do fine. if you struggle at all with math, you won't do well in the class and you'll hate every minute of it. he's a stereotypical, awkward math geek.

For Scientific Calc, he was relatively clear, he related all the mathematics to real-world situations, and was a fair teacher.  He's not the most helpful, but I recommend his class.  He's an average math teacher.

I would rather stab myself in the eye continuously for 100 years than take a class with this man. He's annoying, gives hw that's not based on what you "learned" in class, and is totally unhelpful and even rude when you go to see him. His class is worthless and totally not worth the effort you'll put into it. I guarantee you'll regret taking it.

Stereotpical math geek, but nice.  Not always the most clear, but you could tell he was trying hard.  Tests were easy.  Class room atmosphere was relaxed.  I enjoyed the class and learned a fair amount.
What a putz this guy is!!! I would rather put a hot poker through my eye than have to go to one of his classes again
Just don't take him for a lower class.  I've heard he's good at higher levels, but he's horrid at lower levels.

I am not sure why he has received so many negative comments.  I thought that his classes were highly insightful and I learned a lot from them.  He is always willing to help students outside of class and though his classes are tough - you walk away with a lot.  I highly recommend him - he is one of the best in the department.

probably the worst teacher i've ever had. Completely unwilling to compromise and very disrespectful of his students. His lectures are very unclear and he doesnt spend enough time explaining details and going over examples.  Always runs late. INCREDIBLY unfair and unreasonable grading practices.

Caudill is TERRIBLE.  His tests are wicked hard and he does not cover material well in class. He also doesn't understand the concept of a 50 minute class because EVERY SINGLE CLASS he let us out atleast 5-10 minutes late.  I went to him the day before a test for extra help and he told me flat out th
the reason i quite premed

class is boring and he gives the same notes day after day but tests arent hard, they are exactly what you expect. also, a lot of points avaiable outside of tests, with homework and inclass and out of class projects. i advise to take.

Although this guy seems to have gotten a lot of negative feedback, I can't really understand why.  He tries hard and the lectures make a lot of sense.  He goes over any hard homework and the tests are not very difficult, plus he's really good at helping one on one.

Hard class, and doesn't give much partial credit.  Either you got it or you don't, and nothing inbetween.  He doesn't actually teach how to use the material, just where it came from, which doesn't help understanding the class as much.  Nice guy, and he honestly tries, just teaches the wrong thing.
It's not easy
just don't do it
Hopefully you can teach yourself calc

dr. C's classes are hard, but i learned a ton in both. i'd HIGHLY recommend him - class is fun, interesting, and while it's not the easiest for your gpa, it's definitely worth the intelligence factor.
he is a horrible, horrible teacher. not recommended at all.
Keeping up with work is very important for this class. There is a lot of homework assigned-- three types of it everyday actually. But he explains the ideas well.
Very unhelpful, doesn't explain material very well, takes extreme amount of points off if work is not complete, even if answer is completely right
